conclusion: Journal entry XJ-499 (16 August 2026), described as manual office equipment depreciation, debits Office Equipment (710) AUD 750.00 and GST (820) AUD 75.00 and credits accumulated depreciation (711) AUD 825.00. Account 710 has no prior period trial balance and its current balance of AUD 750.00 comes entirely from XJ-499-1, while the fixed asset register at 30 September 2026 shows Nil, so the entry has no basis and also claims input tax on depreciation. Office Equipment (710) is overstated by AUD 750.00, accumulated depreciation (711) is overstated by AUD 825.00 and the GST liability (820) is understated by AUD 75.00; the three offset, with no effect on profit or loss or net assets.

reasoning_chain.text: XJ-499, posted on 16 August 2026 as 'Being depreciation on office equipment - Manual', debits 710 Office Equipment AUD 750.00 (XJ-499-1), credits 711 accumulated depreciation AUD 825.00 (XJ-499-2) and debits 820 GST AUD 75.00 (XJ-499-3).
Account 710 has no prior period trial balance; its current balance is AUD 750.00, the amount of XJ-499-1.
The fixed asset register at 30 September 2026 shows Nil: the company held no capitalised office equipment, furniture or computer equipment at that date.

The auditor tests the appropriateness of journal entries and other adjustments, including enquiries of the individuals involved about inappropriate or unusual activity in processing them (ASA 240 para 33(a)).
Journal entries processed outside the normal course of business, and entries with little or no explanation, call for examination of their underlying support (ASA 240 para A44).
With no office equipment before or after the entry, XJ-499 records an asset and its depreciation without basis, and the debit to 820 claims input tax on depreciation, which is not an acquisition.

Office Equipment (710) is overstated by AUD 750.00 (75000 cents, the amount of XJ-499-1), accumulated depreciation (711) by AUD 825.00 and the GST liability (820) understated by AUD 75.00; the effects offset, so profit or loss and net assets are not affected.

counter_argument: A purchase invoice for office equipment of AUD 750.00 on or before 16 August 2026, or a register entry for such an asset at 30 September 2026, would show the 710 balance exists.
